issues.description: The migrated frame-mapping loops still spell out the owned iterator’s internal snapshot conversion instead of using the public `it.seq()` specification interface.
issues.rationale: The reviewed revision accesses the complete iterator sequence through `vec::into_iter_elts(it.snapshot@)` in invariants, indexing expressions, and page-size proofs. Verus’s iterator migration guide defines `iter.seq()` as the uniform public interface and specifically replaces iterator-specific snapshot/element representations with `iter.seq()` plus `iter.index()`. The maintainer requested that exact change, and immediate commit 05074fd95721e3e84ed9b950789376c451ec8e17 replaces every raw snapshot conversion in these loops with `it.seq()`. This is an API/migration guideline issue rather than a claim that the raw expression changes runtime behavior. The current reuse-existing-specifications rule supports using the public sequence model here.
issues.verification: source-only; historical Verus was not executed. Checked fixed head 0ba029a82c8d3c9f85af70604d3ed5be7bf84fc7, the complete archived/live discussion, the fixed Verus migration guide at 5727c58567311a1a76dc6bd04451f693b4de0d4d, and immediate commit 05074fd95721e3e84ed9b950789376c451ec8e17 where every raw snapshot conversion is replaced by `it.seq()`.
